outcome: Composite neonatal outcome (umbilical cord artery pH < 7.20, Apgar score < 7 at five minutes, admission to NICU, or neonatal death)
cohort: 140 women who underwent emergency cesarean sections between 2005 and 2009
finding: Obesity was associated with prolonged decision-to-incision and decision-to-delivery intervals during emergency cesarean sections, but not with a difference in neonatal composite outcome.
mod_finding: Obesity was associated with prolonged decision-to-incision and decision-to-delivery intervals during emergency cesarean sections, but not with a difference in neonatal composite outcome.
